layout.hierarchy: The red title overwhelmingly dominates (largest, boldest, most saturated element). The yellow badge is the only other colored element and draws the eye secondarily. The pen icon and black strip are minor. Everything else is empty space.

typography_notes: Title is a bold sans-serif (Arial/Helvetica-like), sentence case ('Transformer Decoder'), very large relative to slide (~40-48pt equivalent), strong red color, horizontally centered. The badge number '50' is a small sans-serif, regular weight, black. No italics, no all-caps, no bullet lists on this slide.
animation_state: No build state visible; this is a static section-divider/title slide. Nothing appears mid-reveal. The pen icon is likely a static cursor overlay from the screen recording, not slide content.
recreation_brief: 1. Create a new 16:9 PowerPoint slide; set the slide background to white (#FFFFFF). 2. Draw a rectangle spanning roughly 5%-95% width and 7%-95% height with no fill (or fill #EBEBEB light gray) and a thin red (#C00000) outline ~1.5pt; this frames the content area. 3. Insert a text box centered horizontally at ~50% width and ~52% height; type 'Transformer Decoder' in Arial Bold, ~44pt, color #C00000, centered alignment. 4. In the top-right corner (about 91% width, 13% height), draw an oval ~0.6in diameter: fill yellow #FFFF66, outline purple #6666CC ~1.5pt; add text '50' in Arial ~12pt black, centered. 5. Optionally add a small gray pen-nib icon (Insert > Icons > pen) at ~54% width, ~76% height, rotated ~45 degrees, colored gray #888888 — or omit if it is judged a cursor artifact. 6. Below the red-bordered rectangle, add a full-width black (#000000) rectangle strip ~4% of slide height at the very bottom to mimic the video frame's bottom bar (optional, only if reproducing the video frame exactly). 7. Leave all remaining space empty; no bullets, images, or charts.
